messages:
Asha Iyer: Drafting a short customer-facing go-live primer focused on prefill/prefetch, batching presets, streaming fallbacks, and renewal-signal capture. Aim: a 1-page handout + 3-line email.
Dmitri Volkov: Sounds good. Keep language non-technical for customers; include one "what we do" sentence and one "what you can check" bullet.
Asha Iyer: Proposed customer opener: "Well prime a small, representative set of your prompts, keep a warm pool for core paths, and automatically fall back to short polling if streaming degrades. Well surface simple checks to you and handle escalation."
Samira Khan: Add a short renewal-risk indicator CS can use: "If weekly active sessions drop >25% compared to baseline for 3 days, schedule a check-in."
Jorge Ramos: For ENG presets, propose three knobs: Latency-first (batch_window_ms=50, max_batch_tokens=512), Balanced (batch_window_ms=150, max_batch_tokens=2048), Cost-first (batch_window_ms=300, max_batch_tokens=4096).
Asha Iyer: Good. Also include a tiny prefill recipe customers can paste:
```
# CUSTOMER PREFILL RECIPE (non-prod first)
prefill_enabled: true
prefill_sample_size: 200
prefill_mode: "staggered"  # immediate | staggered | steady
warm_pool_size: 6
warm_pool_ttl_hours: 72
```
Dmitri Volkov: Observability: give 4 signals and thresholds: `prefill_success_rate` >= 0.9, `kv_cache_hit_rate` >= 0.6, `p50_ttf_token_ms` < 200, `stream_disconnects_per_10k` < 10. If any threshold is breached, trigger the escalation playbook.
Samira Khan: Escalation playbook (customer-facing + internal): 1) CS: confirm sample prompts + re-run prefill in non-prod 2) CS: ask customer to run the short checklist (copyable) 3) ENG: check cache key schema + confirm model + quantization variant 4) ENG oncall: attach trace & raw prompt if still failing.
Asha Iyer: Short customer checklist (copy to email):
- Have you noticed lower response rates or slower responses in the last 72h?
- Can you share 3 recent prompts that exhibit issues?
- Are you using streaming responses in your client? (yes/no)
If yes and you see UI stutters, we may temporarily switch to polling to preserve correctness.
Jorge Ramos: Add a tiny curl example for toggling fallbacks (ENG tech note only, but keep it short):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/fallbacks -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"fallback_mode":"polling","interval_ms":500}'
```
Dmitri Volkov: Also include a one-line note about renewals: "CS should flag accounts where weekly usage < 60% of expected by day 14; treat as renewal-risk and open a health call."
Samira Khan: I'll draft the 3-line customer email: "Hi <Name>, were priming your instance ahead of go-live: weve prefilled common prompts and enabled a warm pool. If you notice slower or missing messages, reply with 3 examples and well investigate."
Asha Iyer: Action items: @Jorge to finalize ENG presets and short curl by Thursday; @Dmitri to confirm final thresholds and PromQL examples; @Samira to draft the customer email and renewal flags. Ill assemble the one-pager and add to CS playbook.
runbook-bot: New runbook created: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/cs/prefill-batch-stream-onepager (access: customer-success, eng).
Jorge Ramos: tiny PromQL for stream disconnects (5m window):
```promql
sum(rate(stream_disconnects_total[5m])) by (service) * 10000
```
Asha Iyer: Lovely. Keep Optimize links out of this one-pager; point customers to Optimize for model/compat recommendations. Planning to publish draft to the CS drive end of day Friday.
Samira Khan: dropping final customer-facing line to set expectations: "Well monitor metrics during the first 72 hours and reach out proactively if we see issues; you can always reply to this thread with examples."
Asha Iyer: Thanks team. If anything else, drop it here and Ill fold into the final one-pager. :white_check_mark:
